meta_title: Animated Safety Videos | 2D & 3D Safety Animation | TECH EHS
meta_description: 2D and 3D safety animation for inductions, SOPs, incident recreation and technical training, scripted by EHS experts and voiced in 40+ languages for your sites.
h1: Safety videos your workforce watches, understands and remembers
definition: TECH EHS animated safety videos are custom 2D and 3D animations, scripted by EHS specialists, that explain hazards, procedures, incidents and site rules visually so workers of any language or literacy level can understand and follow them.
hero_sub: We turn your SOPs, incident reports and site rules into short animated films, recreating your actual plant, equipment and PPE without stopping production for a film crew.

problem.title: Why classroom slides and long manuals don't change behavior
problem.intro: Most frontline safety communication still relies on text-heavy procedures and presentations delivered in one language. Workers sign attendance sheets, but the message rarely reaches the task.

points.title: Multilingual, mixed-literacy workforces
points.text: Contract crews on a single site may speak five or more languages, and a written procedure in English protects few of them.

points.title: Hazards you cannot film
points.text: Toxic releases, arc flash, falls and confined space engulfment cannot be shown safely with a camera, so they are explained in words instead of shown.

points.title: Lessons from incidents fade fast
points.text: Investigation reports are filed and forgotten, and the same failure repeats at another site because nobody saw how it actually happened.

features_title: What our safety animation studio produces
features_intro: Every project is scripted by people who have worked in EHS, reviewed by your subject matter experts and built around your own sites, equipment and procedures.

features.title: 2D and 3D safety animation
features.text: Choose clean 2D motion graphics for rules and concepts, or detailed 3D for equipment, plant layouts and step-by-step tasks, or combine both in one film.

features.title: Incident and near miss recreation
features.text: Rebuild an incident from the investigation report, showing the sequence of events, failed barriers and root causes without naming individuals.

features.title: SOP and work instruction videos
features.text: Convert standard operating procedures into short task videos that show each step, critical control and PPE requirement in the right order.

features.title: Induction for employees, contractors and visitors
features.text: Site-specific induction films covering site rules, emergency routes, assembly points and restricted areas, ready to plug into your induction system.

features.title: Multilingual voiceover and subtitles
features.text: Professional voice artists and translated on-screen text in 40+ languages*, including Hindi, Arabic, Tagalog, Bengali, Spanish and Portuguese.

features.title: LMS-ready delivery
features.text: Delivered as MP4 for screens and toolbox talks, or packaged as SCORM with quiz questions so completions are tracked in your LMS.

steps.title: Brief and script
steps.text: We review your procedures, incident reports and site photos, then an EHS scriptwriter drafts the narration and learning objectives for your approval.

steps.title: Storyboard and style frames
steps.text: Each scene is sketched with characters, equipment and camera angles, and you sign off the look before any animation starts.

steps.title: Animation and voiceover
steps.text: Our 2D and 3D artists build the scenes and recreate your site, while voice artists record the narration in each language you need.

steps.title: Review, revise and deliver
steps.text: You review a full draft with timestamped comments, we apply revisions, and final files are delivered as MP4, SCORM or both.

outcomes_title: What clients typically see after switching to animation

outcomes.label: Better knowledge retention
outcomes.text: Visual demonstrations of hazards stay with workers longer than slides or verbal briefings.

outcomes.label: Shorter induction time
outcomes.text: A 10-minute animated induction replaces a much longer classroom session for visitors and contractors.

outcomes.label: Lower cost than live filming
outcomes.text: No shutdowns, film crews, actors or permits needed to show high-hazard scenarios.

standards_title: Content aligned with the standards your training must meet

comparison.title: Animation vs. live-action safety filming
rows: Cannot safely stage fires, falls or releases
Any scenario shown accurately and safely

Cutaways show internal flows, pressures and failure points

faqs.a: They are short 2D or 3D animated films that explain hazards, procedures, site rules or incidents visually, so workers can see what to do and why without relying on written text.
2D suits rules, concepts and behavioral messages and is faster to produce. 3D suits equipment, plant layouts and tasks where workers need to recognize the real environment. Many projects mix both.

faqs.q: How long does a typical safety animation take to produce?
faqs.a: A 2 to 4 minute video usually takes 3 to 6 weeks* from approved brief to final delivery, depending on 3D complexity, number of languages and review cycles.

faqs.q: Can you recreate our actual site and equipment?
faqs.a: Yes. We build scenes from your photos, drawings, P&IDs or CAD models, and match your PPE, signage, uniforms and color codes.

faqs.q: Which languages do you offer for voiceover?
faqs.a: We offer professional voiceover and subtitles in 40+ languages*, including English, Hindi, Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Tagalog, Bengali, Tamil and Urdu.

faqs.q: Can the videos be tracked in our LMS?
faqs.a: Yes. Videos can be packaged as SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004 with optional quizzes, or delivered through the TECH EHS e-learning and induction platforms.

cta.title: Turn your next procedure into a film people remember
cta.text: Send us one SOP, incident report or induction deck and we will propose a script outline, style and timeline.
